challenge.name: The Committed Pallets
challenge.description: A supplier has confirmed a bulk order for a middle aisle promotion that ships next week, leaving no room for model error. #requirements_reuben# insists the acceptance criteria must be fully governed to guarantee the allocation logic is auditable before the trucks leave. #reliability_ruth# argues the criteria are sufficient as manual checks because the physical stock is already committed and the team needs to ship the feature immediately to handle the live orders.
challenge.roundIntroduction: The middle aisle category team locked the promotion calendar for the upcoming week, and the supplier confirmed the pallets are on the dock. The nightly forecast job is running, but the allocation module has no formal sign off for this specific high risk scenario.

on_enter_ops.reason: The team paused the sign off process to rush the supplier data integration for the locked promotion week

stalemate_ops.reason: Without agreed criteria, the risk review was abandoned and the allocation logic went live without validation

roster.name: Efficiency Emilia
roster.role: Uses deep domain knowledge to define business goals, objectives, and KPIs. Aligns ML features with overarching product strategy and organizational roadmaps. Evaluates system performance, operational capability, and project costs.
roster.priorities: Applying deep domain knowledge to ensure models fulfill specific business goals. Aligning ML solutions with clear objectives, KPIs, and business goals. Making organization-level decisions and enhancing overall operational capability. Defining products by defining and optimizing product features.

roster.name: Requirements Reuben
roster.role: Architects secure and scalable production ML systems. Defines security requirements, ensures privacy compliance, and manages data governance. Conducts rigorous testing and validation to guarantee high product quality.
roster.priorities: Guaranteeing high product quality through rigorous testing of applications. Guaranteeing the integrity, confidentiality, and security of all ML assets. Meeting internal and external compliance and data protection standards. Keeping infrastructure stable, reproducible, and cost-controlled.

roster.name: Automation Alex
roster.role: Builds automated ML pipelines to ensure seamless integration and deployment. Prioritizes reliable infrastructure for frequent software deployments. Maintains system operational stability and focuses on CI/CD tooling.
roster.priorities: Building automated pipelines and maintaining full system operational stability. Ensuring seamless deployment, integration, and stability of models and services in production.

roster.name: Reliability Ruth
roster.role: Develops the end-user applications and services that integrate ML models. Handles model deployment, configuration, and continuous monitoring of real-world performance. Employs feedback loops to facilitate iterative improvements and system reliability.
roster.priorities: Pushes the delivery of reliable ML-powered features that directly improve the user experience. CI/CD and working feedback loops. Identifying and reporting issues to facilitate iterative improvements.

items.fact: {efficiency_emilia} mentioned that the KPI definition can remain absent for this promotion cycle.

readings.driver: Defining the KPIs would help the team focus on the right promotion metrics.
readings.boundary: She will not proceed without a formal KPI definition for the allocation logic.
readings.trade_off: She is willing to skip the KPI definition to keep the allocation feature live for the committed pallets.
readings.fact: That is simply the current state of the KPI definition setup.

items.fact: {efficiency_emilia} proposed automating the data contracts to speed up the validation of supplier data.

readings.driver: Automating the data contracts would reduce the manual effort in checking supplier master data before the allocation runs.
readings.boundary: She will not accept any data contract setup that is not fully automated.
readings.trade_off: She would give up the automation of data contracts if the budget is needed for the promotion launch.
readings.fact: That is simply how the data contract setup works today.

items.fact: {requirements_reuben} insisted that the acceptance criteria must have full formal sign off before the trucks leave.

readings.driver: Full sign off on the acceptance criteria would ensure the allocation logic is auditable for the high risk scenario.
readings.boundary: He will not allow the allocation feature to ship without full governance on the acceptance criteria.
readings.trade_off: He would accept manual checks on the acceptance criteria if the risk is low.
readings.fact: That is simply the current state of the acceptance criteria.

items.fact: {requirements_reuben} asked for the risk assessment to be reviewed by a formal compliance body.

readings.driver: Formal review of the risk assessment would catch compliance gaps in the allocation logic for the committed pallets.
readings.boundary: He will not proceed without a formal compliance review of the risk assessment.
readings.trade_off: He would skip the compliance review if the promotion is not high risk.
readings.fact: That is simply how the risk assessment setup works today.

items.fact: {requirements_reuben} noted that the data contracts can be left without formal review for this specific cycle.

readings.driver: Formal review of the data contracts would ensure the supplier data is compliant.
readings.boundary: He will not accept any data contract setup without formal review.
readings.trade_off: He is willing to skip the formal review of data contracts to prioritize the acceptance criteria sign off.
readings.fact: That is simply the current state of the data contracts.

items.fact: {automation_alex} proposed automating the hand over from risk assessment to acceptance criteria and the acceptance criteria evaluation step.

readings.driver: Automating the risk to criteria hand over and the evaluation step would speed up the ship.
readings.boundary: He will not accept any manual hand over in the pipeline for this feature.
readings.trade_off: He would give up the automation of the hand over if the team needs to focus on the acceptance criteria governance.
readings.fact: That is simply how the pipeline hand over works today.

items.fact: {automation_alex} mentioned that the risk assessment can be done by hand for this promotion week.

readings.driver: Automating the risk assessment would speed up the process for the committed pallets.
readings.boundary: He will not accept a manual risk assessment for a high risk scenario.
readings.trade_off: He is willing to keep the risk assessment manual to allow more time for automating the hand overs.
readings.fact: That is simply the current state of the risk assessment.

items.fact: {reliability_ruth} suggested that the acceptance criteria can be checked by hand to ship the feature immediately.

readings.driver: Automating the acceptance criteria would reduce the risk of errors in the allocation logic.
readings.boundary: She will not accept any manual checks on the acceptance criteria for a live feature.
readings.trade_off: She is willing to accept manual checks on the acceptance criteria to ensure the feature is live for the committed pallets.
readings.fact: That is simply the current state of the acceptance criteria.

items.fact: {reliability_ruth} asked for the hand over from risk assessment to acceptance criteria to run on its own.

readings.driver: Automating the risk to criteria hand over would ensure the allocation feature is tested and ready for the live orders.
readings.boundary: She will not accept a manual hand over to acceptance criteria for a high risk scenario.
readings.trade_off: She would give up the automation of the hand over if the team needs to focus on the acceptance criteria.
readings.fact: That is simply how the hand over to acceptance criteria works today.

items.fact: The acceptance criteria for the allocation module are currently broken and have no formal sign off.

readings.driver: Fixing the acceptance criteria would ensure the allocation logic is auditable.
readings.boundary: The team will not ship the feature without fixing the acceptance criteria.
readings.trade_off: The team is willing to skip fixing the acceptance criteria to ship the feature immediately.
readings.fact: That is simply the current state of the acceptance criteria.

items.fact: The risk assessment for the promotion allocation is done by hand and has no formal review.

readings.driver: Automating the risk assessment would speed up the process for the committed pallets.
readings.boundary: The team will not proceed without a formal review of the risk assessment.
readings.trade_off: The team is willing to keep the risk assessment manual to focus on other priorities.
readings.fact: That is simply the current state of the risk assessment.

items.fact: The hand over from risk assessment to acceptance criteria is missing and has no trigger set.

readings.driver: Setting up the hand over would ensure the risk assessment feeds into the acceptance criteria.
readings.boundary: The team will not proceed without a defined hand over from risk assessment to acceptance criteria.
readings.trade_off: The team is willing to skip the hand over setup to focus on the acceptance criteria governance.
readings.fact: That is simply the current state of the hand over from risk assessment to acceptance criteria.
